Performers
The Danish String Quartet (string quartet) Documented

The Commons file and the video name the ensemble only. The individual players of this 2015 concert are not listed in the sources consulted, so no names are inferred.

[1] [2] [3]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The performing edition and any editorial choices are not identified in the recording sources. The performance appears to omit the first-movement exposition repeat, which is an observation from the audio, not a documented fact.

[1]
Recorded
May 2015 Documented

The uploader’s video description gives the concert as May 2015. The Commons date, 24 July 2015, is the YouTube upload date, not a session date.

[2]
Place
Tel Aviv Museum of Art, Tel Aviv, Israel Documented

Stated in the video description. The video is titled “Haydn Quartet Op. 54 No. 2, Danish String Quartet LIVE”; the description misprints the opus as 64.

[2]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

The video description credits Gilad Shabani for the video and Ilan Rechtman as music director of the concert series; neither is credited for extracting the audio. A Commons uploader’s username is not a transfer credit.

[2] [1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is documented; the Commons date 2015-07-24 is the YouTube upload date.

[1]
Processing
Audio taken from the YouTube concert video and stored on Commons as an Ogg Vorbis file, which Commons transcodes to an MP3 derivative. Documented

The Commons file is one of four movement extracts from a single 19-minute video; who made the cuts, and whether any editing or loudness processing was applied, is not stated.

[1]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Haydn died in 1809. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

[5] [6]
Recording rights
Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 (the Commons {{YouTube CC-BY}} template): an explicit release of the recording for any use with attribution. Documented

This is rule 1 of the programme’s rights rule, an explicit recording release. The Commons file page records the YouTube CC-BY status of the source video. The sources do not show who applied that setting; it is taken to be the channel owner who posted the concert film, and it covers the video as posted.
